The referendum of 28 September 1958 on de Gaulle's French Community, in which Guinea alone among the French African colonies voted No, by about 95 percent. Guinea became independent on 2 October 1958.

Sekou Toure had told de Gaulle in Conakry that Guinea preferred poverty in freedom to riches in slavery. France left at once, pulling out officials and taking or wrecking equipment, and Guinea turned to the Soviet bloc and to Nkrumah's Ghana for help. Its example showed that full independence was possible, and in 1960 the rest of French West Africa followed.
sum: The referendum of 28 September 1958 on de Gaulle's French Community, in which Guinea alone among the French African colonies voted No, by about 95 percent. Guinea became independent on 2 October 1958.
